title: sales-partnership-scratch-notes-novadocs
content:
Account: NovaDocs (YC S20) - clinical documentation startup

Quick context:
- Builds structured clinical notes from voice + EHR signals. Selling to mid-size clinics and hospital groups.
- Headcount ~65, raised Series B 2024. Focus on productizing note quality and reducing clinician documentation time.
- Tech: inference-heavy (real-time/near-real-time voice -> notes), inferences per session ~100-500 tokens, peak concurrency around EOD for batch uploads.

Why Redwood might fit:
- Latency + cost matter: doctors need near-real-time transcripts and async post-editing.
- Private deployment ask: they mentioned HIPAA concerns on sales call -> Private (VPC) or Dedicated recommended.
- Value props to emphasize: deterministic latency, predictable pricing for high concurrency, audit logs + KMS for PHI, can run on-prem or VPC.

Key stakeholders (from LinkedIn / notes):
- Maya Gupta (Head of ML) - leads model infra and production models (likely technical champion)
- Aaron Blake (CTO) - cares about security, compliance, ops overhead
- Priya Menon (VP Product) - product owners for clinician workflows; cares about accuracy and UX
- Sales/Procurement: Rajiv Kapoor - procurement and contracting

Tech signals / hints from website / job postings:
- Hiring ML infra engineers (mentions "low-latency serving")
- Uses AWS, some on-prem integrations (EKSesque)
- Currently running a mix of open-source models + finetuned proprietary models for clinical phrasing

Primary use cases to pitch:
1) Real-time voice -> structured note generation (low latency SLOs)
2) Batch post-processing for quality/regression monitoring (cost-sensitive)
3) PII/PHI controls + audit trails for compliance

Pain / triggers to surface in discovery:
- Is model latency causing clinician friction? Specific SLA they want?
- Are they hitting cost spikes during month-end or EHR syncs?
- Any blockers for moving off their current vendor (data residency, encryption, integration)?

Discovery questions (short):
- What is your target 95th percentile latency for live sessions?
- Typical tokens per session and concurrent sessions at peak?
- Which data residency / compliance constraints are absolute vs negotiable?
- How do you currently measure note quality? Any evals/prompts we can see?
- Do you need streaming partial responses for UX?

Outbound email drafts (A/B) - keep short, personalized:
Subject A: quick q about reducing clinician docs time at NovaDocs
Subject B: Maya \u2014 latency + PHI controls for NovaDocs?

Email short (cold):
Hi Maya,

I saw NovaDocs is shipping voice-first clinical notes for hospitals \u2014 impressive. We help teams like yours get consistent, low-latency LLM inference with VPC/KMS controls so you can meet HIPAA SLAs without a big ops lift.

Would you be open to a 20-min intro to see if we can cut processing time spikes or reduce inference spend while keeping model quality?


shley

Email longer (more technical):
Hi Maya,

Quick note \u2014 at Redwood we run a unified inference stack for hosted, dedicated and private deployments. For companies processing PHI we typically recommend a private deployment (VPC + KMS + audit logs) and use serving/runtime knobs (quantization, smart batching, prefix caching) to cut per-token cost 2-4x while keeping 95th% latency predictable.

If helpful I can share a short case study (anonymized) showing a 40% cost reduction and consistent 200-300ms 95th for live sessions. Would you be open to 20 min next week?

Thanks,
Ashley Patel

Cold call opener (30s):
"Hi Maya, this is Ashley from Redwood Inference \u2014 we help voice-first clinical note teams get consistent, low-latency model serving with private deployments for PHI. Curious if performance or cost has been a blocker for you lately?"

Objection handling (common):
- "We already have infra / too complex": Ask about pain points (ops time, unpredictable costs). Offer baseline benchmark and PoC plan that uses lightweight dedicated capacity.
- "Security / HIPAA concerns": Emphasize Private deployments, customer-managed KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC2 + compliance pack. Offer redacted architecture diagram and security questionnaire.
- "Cost" / "We run cheaper with spot instances": Explain unit economics for inference vs build cost (engine optimizations, prefix caching, autoscaling). Offer cost model run with their metrics.
- "Latency isn't a problem": Probe deeper \u2014 are tail latencies spiking during specific workflows? Offer a short latency audit (1-week trace).

Notes for PoC / pilot proposal:
- Minimal pilot: 2 weeks, small subset of traffic (nightly batch + 10% live routing). Measure token cost, 95/99 latency, and clinician edit reduction.
- Deliverables: latency/cost dashboards, security questionnaire, one-pager on integration steps.
- Runbook: rollback to their current endpoints, automatic fallback to baseline model, canary traffic routing.

Suggested collateral to send:
- One-pager: "Redwood for regulated workloads" (Confluence-2453)
- Case study: anonymized hospital customer (internal)
- Security package: SOC2 + KMS architecture + data flow diagram

Next steps / TODOs:
- Draft short intro email and send to Maya + Aaron (cc Rajiv) \u2014 A/B test subject lines (send Mon AM)
- Ask Danielle for anonymized case study slides to attach
- Run quick internal calc: estimate tokens/session * price tiers -> put in email as "ballpark monthly cost"
- Prepare 1-page pilot scope and slide deck (to share on intro call)

Meeting agenda (20 min):
- 3 min intros & context
- 5 min current infra + pain points (latency, cost, security)
- 6 min propose Redwood approach + pilot outline
- 4 min next steps / timeline

Random scratch notes / reminders:
- Bring up streaming partial responses (helps editing speed)
- Ask if they finetune models on PHI \u2014 mention redwood supports model variants & rollouts
- If procurement asks: highlight Dedicated pricing model and enterprise contract options

---
End of note.
